title: Area of Triangles and Parallelograms
seo_title: Year 7 Area of Triangles and Parallelograms Worksheets: Base × Height and Missing Lengths (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: solve problems involving the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas and appropriate units
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on the area of triangles and parallelograms for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7M01): diagrams, missing base or height, composite shapes and practical problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Parallelogram area = base × height. Triangle area = ½ × base × height.
key_sub: Always use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.
body_html:
How it works

A parallelogram can be cut and rearranged into a rectangle, so its area = base × perpendicular height.

A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height, so its area = ½ × base × perpendicular height.

The height must be perpendicular (at right angles) to the base. Slanted sides are not used for area.

Example

Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm.

½ × 10 × 6 = 30.

Answer: 30 cm²

Example

Find the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm, slanted side 5 cm and height 4 cm.

9 × 4 = 36. Do not use the 5 cm.

Answer: 36 cm²

Example

A triangle has area 24 cm² and base 8 cm. Find its height.

½ × 8 × h = 24, so 4h = 24.

Answer: 6 cm

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to halve for a triangle: base × height gives double the area.
  • Halving for a parallelogram. Only triangles have the ½.
  • Using the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height.
  • Writing cm instead of cm² for an area.

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
What is the formula for the area of a parallelogram?
faq.a: Area = base × perpendicular height. It is a rectangle that has been pushed over.

faq.q: Why is a triangle half of a parallelogram?
faq.a: Two identical triangles fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height.

faq.q: How do I find the height if I know the area?
faq.a: Work backwards. For a triangle with area 24 cm² and base 8 cm: ½ × 8 × h = 24, so h = 6 cm.

items.q: A triangular sail has a base of 3 m and a perpendicular height of 5 m. What is its area?
A garden bed is a parallelogram with base 6 m and perpendicular height 2.5 m. What is its area?
A triangle and a parallelogram have the same base and the same perpendicular height. How do their areas compare?
c: The triangle is half the parallelogram
items.e: Triangle: ½ × b × h. Parallelogram: b × h. The triangle is half the parallelogram.

items.q: A road sign is a triangle with base 90 cm and perpendicular height 78 cm. What is its area?

A parallelogram has sides 8 cm and 5 cm and a perpendicular height of 4 cm (to the 8 cm base). What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 8 × 4 = 32 cm². The 5 cm side is not used.

items.q: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is its area?
items.e: The two shorter sides are at right angles, so they are the base and height: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm².

items.q: Which units are used for area?
items.e: Area is measured in square units such as cm² and m².

items.q: How many cm² are in 1 m²?
A triangle has area 18 cm². Which could be its base and perpendicular height?
items.e: ½ × 9 × 4 = 18 cm². The others give 9, 9 and 9 cm².

items.q: A rhombus-shaped tile is a parallelogram with base 15 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. How many tiles cover 1.8 m²?

A parallelogram is cut along its height and the triangle moved to the other end. What shape does it make?
c: A rectangle with the same area
A triangle with half the area
A trapezium with a bigger area
A square with double the area
items.e: The pieces make a rectangle with the same area: base × height. That is why parallelogram area = base × height.

items.q: Two triangles each have base 10 cm. One has height 4 cm and the other 6 cm. What is their total area?
A kite is made of two triangles, each with base 40 cm and height 25 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Each triangle: ½ × 40 × 25 = 500 cm². Two: 1000 cm².
